docs/internals/open-source-licenses.md:28-31 (build fails without a distributable license identifier or notice text; SPDX templates)

SUS-1.note: Several named maintainers and a company sponsor. No CODEOWNERS and no governance or succession document. History could not be measured in a shallow clone.

SUS-2.note: Templates, a required CI check and an automated triage and review pipeline are in place. Whether human approval is required before merge is set outside the repo and could not be verified. No code-owner review or signed-commit requirement.

evidence: AGENTS.md:1-187 (agent instructions; PR bodies end with the model and harness)
CONTRIBUTING.md:102-110,116-117 (model acceptance policy, checked during triage)
command: git log -1 -> HEAD 7e289ae1 carries 'Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5'
AGENTS.md:41 (most contributions come from T3 Code itself)
SUS-3.note: How agents contribute and how their work is triaged and reviewed is disclosed, and attribution is requested and checked by automated triage. Agent contributions are not evaluated over time (e.g. defect rate by model).

gaps.title: Agents run unsandboxed with approvals off by default
gaps.case: packages/contracts/src/providerPolicy.ts:32 sets DEFAULT_RUNTIME_MODE = 'full-access'. CodexAdapterV2.ts:709-716 maps it to approvalPolicy 'never' with sandbox dangerFullAccess, and ClaudeAdapterV2.ts:2006-2039 maps it to bypassPermissions. docs/user/permission-modes.md:8 confirms Full access is the initial default. T3 adds no OS boundary of its own; AgentScope only sets memory limits, and only on Linux.
gaps.impact: Excessive agency (OWASP LLM06): instructions injected through repository files, web pages or tool output can run commands and change files with no human checkpoint. Remote control from phones and the relay widens who can start such runs.
gaps.fix: Default new installs and new projects to Supervised or Auto (provider review). Require an explicit per-project opt-in to Full access, with a visible warning. Offer an OS-level boundary (container or egress allowlist) through the existing AgentScope.wrap hook.

gaps.title: Telemetry is on by default, opt-out is env-var only, and the UI calls linkable ids 'anonymous'
gaps.case: apps/server/src/telemetry/AnalyticsService.ts:81 defaults T3CODE_TELEMETRY_ENABLED to true. docs/user/telemetry.md:16-22 offers only an environment variable to opt out. WelcomeWizard.tsx:435 says 'anonymous usage data', while Identify.ts:181-189,255-268 reads ~/.codex/auth.json (id_token) and ~/.claude.json to derive owner ids, hashed with unsalted SHA-256 (telemetryId.ts:8-9). There is no DO_NOT_TRACK support and no settings toggle (rg).
gaps.impact: GDPR consent and transparency risk: pseudonymous, linkable account identifiers leave the machine by default, and the in-app wording understates this. Desktop users on Windows must set a user environment variable to opt out.
gaps.fix: Offer a first-run choice and a Settings toggle, honour DO_NOT_TRACK, and call the data pseudonymous. Replace unsalted hashes of provider account ids with a keyed hash or a random per-install id, and stop reading provider credential files for analytics identity.

gaps.title: Mutable action references in credentialed jobs; no dependency update or vulnerability scanning
gaps.case: Only 20 of 116 third-party action references are SHA-pinned (probe ci.pinned_actions). mobile-eas-preview.yml:100-102 runs expo/expo-github-action/continuous-deploy-fingerprint@main with EXPO_TOKEN. release.yml:705,860,876 uses softprops/action-gh-release@v3 in the contents:write release job, and ci.yml:426 uses dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable. There is no Dependabot or Renovate configuration and no audit or OSV step in any workflow.
gaps.impact: Supply-chain compromise: a moved upstream tag or branch executes in jobs that hold release, store or signing credentials, and known-vulnerable dependencies are never flagged.
gaps.fix: Pin every third-party action to a full commit SHA and let a bot update the pins. Add Renovate or Dependabot for npm, cargo and actions, a vulnerability gate (OSV-Scanner or pnpm audit), and OpenSSF Scorecard.

gaps.title: Release binaries have no provenance or signed checksums, and signing is silently optional
gaps.case: release.yml:752-765 writes SHA256SUMS unsigned. scripts/install.sh:194-206, scripts/install.ps1:171-186 and scripts/npm-launcher/t3.mjs:75-91 check archives only against SHA256SUMS from the same release. release-desktop.yml:446-486 logs 'signing disabled' and continues when secrets are missing, and docs/operations/release.md:58 calls signing optional. npm --provenance (release.yml:927) covers only the launcher, not the executables it downloads.
gaps.impact: All install and self-update paths (curl|sh, npx t3, t3 update, boot service, SSH environments) prove integrity but not authenticity. A tampered release asset or account would pass, and a misconfigured secret can ship an unsigned stable build.
gaps.fix: Attest the archives and installers (GitHub artifact attestations or Sigstore) and sign SHA256SUMS. Verify the signature in install.sh, install.ps1, the npm launcher and t3 update. Fail stable and nightly releases when signing secrets are absent.

gaps.title: MCP tool catalog is large and unmeasured
gaps.case: There are 83 Tool.make definitions under apps/server/src/mcp (non-test), with at least 38,362 characters of description text before JSON-schema structure (33,550 in toolkits/*/tools.ts, 4,812 in packages/contracts MCP schemas). All toolkits are registered on one endpoint for every provider session (docs/orchestration-v2/orchestrator-mcp-server.md:36-37), and no test measures tools/list size.
gaps.impact: Each provider session pays an estimated 9.6k+ tokens of catalog per turn (at 4 characters per token), large menus degrade tool selection, and catalog regressions go unseen.
gaps.fix: Measure tools/list bytes in CI with a budget, next to the existing transfer budgets. Register the preview, device and pull-request toolkits only when the session can use them, and shorten descriptions.

gaps.title: No per-task budgets for agent runs, delegations or schedules
gaps.case: Searching apps/server/src and packages/contracts/src for maxTurns, tokenBudget, costLimit or turnTimeout finds only the Codex goal tokenBudget passthrough (CodexAdapterV2.ts:940). delegate_task and scheduled tasks take no budget (docs/orchestration-v2/orchestrator-mcp-server.md:225-260), and usage is reported only after the fact (docs/user/usage.md:7-14).
gaps.impact: Unbounded consumption (OWASP LLM10): delegated, scheduled or webhook-triggered agents can loop until provider subscription limits stop them, and cost becomes visible only afterwards.
gaps.fix: Add token, wall-clock and call budgets to the runtime policy for runs, delegated tasks and schedules, enforce them in the orchestrator, and report spend against the budget per run.

gaps.title: Headline claims have no source, method or date
gaps.case: README.md:3 says 'best-in-class mobile app' and README.md:11 'performant'. AGENTS.md:9 says 'over 500,000 users'. apps/marketing/src/lib/site.ts:9-12 hard-codes users '500,000' and githubStars '24k+', which index.astro:119 renders.
gaps.impact: People and agents choosing tools from descriptions get claims they cannot check, and the hard-coded counts drift silently.
gaps.fix: Derive the user count from the analytics pipeline with method and date, or remove it. Link performance claims to the CI transfer-budget report, and drop unsupported superlatives.

gaps.title: No SBOM, support period or CRA position for a widely distributed product
gaps.case: Probe ci.sbom found no SBOM generation. .github/SECURITY.md:1-8 lists no supported versions, and probe evo.support found no support period. rg finds no mention of the Cyber Resilience Act, AI Act or Accessibility Act in docs or the marketing site. The product ships through the App Store, Google Play, npm, winget, scoop, brew and AUR.
gaps.impact: CRA vulnerability reporting applies from 11 Sep 2026, and SBOM and support-period duties from 11 Dec 2027. Enterprise buyers and downstream packagers lack component and support data.
gaps.fix: Emit CycloneDX or SPDX SBOMs per release from the existing license-manifest generator. State supported versions and a security-support period in SECURITY.md, and document the CRA role and obligations.

gaps.title: Accessibility and localisation are untested in a UI shipped to app stores
gaps.case: Probe ui.i18n found no i18n library or translation files. rg finds no axe, pa11y or lighthouse in the repo, although the web suite already runs Vitest browser tests in Chromium in CI (ci.yml:255-300).
gaps.impact: Screen-reader and keyboard regressions go undetected, non-English users are unsupported, and consumer-facing distribution carries EAA exposure.
gaps.fix: Add axe checks to the existing *.browser.test.tsx suites for key screens, move UI strings into a message catalogue, and state the accessibility conformance target.

gaps.title: No CODEOWNERS or governance for a codebase mostly written by agents
gaps.case: There is no .github/CODEOWNERS (probe meta.codeowners) and no governance file. AGENTS.md:41 says most contributions come from T3 Code itself. The only required check visible in the repo is the 'Check' job (ci.yml:494-496), and review requirements are not visible.
gaps.impact: Security-critical paths (apps/server/src/auth, apps/server/src/mcp, .github/workflows, release scripts) have no enforced owner review, and continuity rests on a small named group.
gaps.fix: Add CODEOWNERS for the auth, MCP, relay, release and workflow paths, require code-owner review there, and write a short governance and succession note.

gaps.title: MCP error contract drifts from its docs and has no retry semantics
gaps.case: packages/contracts/src/orchestratorMcp.ts:671-692 defines 16 failure codes. docs/orchestration-v2/orchestrator-mcp-server.md:509-524 lists 14, missing thread_credential_required and target_required. OrchestratorMcpFailure carries only code and message, while provider and VCS errors carry retryable (orchestrationV2.ts:1261, vcs.ts:122).
gaps.impact: Agents cannot tell from the contract which MCP failures to retry, and documented error handling misses real codes.
gaps.fix: Generate the code table from the schema, checked in CI, and add retryable plus an optional remediation field to OrchestratorMcpFailure.

gaps.title: Design index presents the shipped durable outbox as future work
gaps.case: docs/orchestration-v2/README.md:110-166 ('Tracked Follow-Up: Durable Effect Outbox') says the current pipeline uses reactors. apps/server/src/orchestration-v2/EffectOutbox.ts ships the outbox, and AGENTS.md:154 describes it as current.
gaps.impact: Maintainers and coding agents reading the design index get the wrong side-effect and recovery architecture.
gaps.fix: Rewrite or remove the section, as the project's own rule in AGENTS.md 'Documentation' requires ('rewrite or remove the affected text').

opportunities.title: One untrusted-content envelope for every injection channel
opportunities.description: T3 frames untrusted text in four ways: nonce-tagged blocks for webhooks, a JSON-encoded frame for captured windows, and prose preambles for transcripts and thread references. Standardising on the nonce-tagged envelope, with redaction and provenance fields, and publishing it with its tests would give one tested format and a shared injection corpus to pi, Orca and PandaCode, which also feed external content to agents.

opportunities.title: Capability-scoped MCP toolkits with a catalog budget
opportunities.description: Advertise only the toolkits a session can use: preview and device tools when a browser or device is attached, pull-request tools when a source-control account is linked. Add a tools/list byte budget to CI next to the transfer budgets. Baseline: 83 tools and at least 38,362 characters of descriptions.

opportunities.title: Turn the license-manifest generator into per-release SBOMs
opportunities.description: The build already walks the production dependency closure for web, server, desktop and mobile, and fails when license data is missing. Emitting CycloneDX or SPDX from the same walk, attested with the release, covers the CRA SBOM duty (Dec 2027) and SEC-4 at low cost.

opportunities.title: Run Full-access agents inside agent-sandbox-lockdown-style boundaries via AgentScope.wrap
opportunities.description: Every provider launch already goes through AgentScope.wrap, which today adds systemd memory scopes on Linux. agent-sandbox-lockdown ships the missing boundary: DNS and egress-proxy allowlists, least-privilege tools, a step cap, a JSONL tool log and a kill switch. Composing the two gives Full-access sessions an OS-level boundary without changing provider adapters, and closes the main AGT-2 gap.

opportunities.title: Shared adapter conformance kit for coding-agent GUIs
opportunities.description: T3, Orca and PandaCode all wrap the same CLIs (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi). T3 has the strongest verification asset: a provider-neutral replay runtime (packages/provider-testing), the ProviderAdapterV2 contract with capability records (packages/provider-core), recorders for six providers, and 91 recorded scenarios (149 NDJSON transcripts, 8.0 MB). Publishing them as a versioned conformance suite would let each GUI test adapters against the same recorded behaviour and catch provider protocol drift once for all of them. Today both packages are private and coupled to Effect v4.

opportunities.title: Extract the SQLite durable command and effect kernel
opportunities.description: EventSink, CommandReceiptStore and EffectOutbox form a compact, local-first durable-execution core: one-transaction commit, leased claims, replay-safe versus process-bound effect classes, process-loss reconciliation and a restart-chain cap. absurd covers the same ground on Postgres, and pi-durable at the agent-conversation level. A shared contract for these semantics, with T3's kernel as the SQLite implementation, would let harnesses reuse proven crash semantics instead of reimplementing them. The effect-type registry must be split from orchestration types first.

opportunities.title: Fetch vendored reference trees on demand instead of committing them
opportunities.description: 21,835 of 28,433 tracked files (77%, 218 MB on disk) are git subtrees under .repos/ that agents read as references. Every CI job sparse-excludes them, and scripts/sync-reference-repos.ts already syncs them at pinned refs. Fetching them on demand at those pins keeps the agent benefit while shrinking clones and code-search noise.

reengineering.component: Release and CI supply chain (.github/workflows/*, scripts/install.sh, scripts/install.ps1, scripts/npm-launcher/t3.mjs, packages/shared/src/cliRelease.ts)
reengineering.gain: Authenticity, not just integrity, on every install and self-update path, and no mutable third-party code in credentialed jobs.
reengineering.measure: SHA-pinned third-party action refs go from 20/116 to 116/116 (rqs probe ci.pinned_actions). All release assets carry attestations (from 0). An installer test rejects a tampered SHA256SUMS. A stable release fails when signing secrets are absent.

reengineering.component: Safe defaults: packages/contracts/src/providerPolicy.ts:32 (runtime mode), apps/server/src/telemetry/AnalyticsService.ts:81 and Identify.ts (telemetry consent and identity)
reengineering.gain: Least agency and consent by default, without removing any capability.
reengineering.measure: A contract test asserts the default runtime mode is not full-access. Track the share of new threads started in Full access (existing feature.used analytics). AnalyticsService tests cover the toggle and DO_NOT_TRACK. PRV-1 and AGT-2 re-scored at 3 or higher.

reengineering.component: Largest modules: Orchestrator.ts (12,143 lines), ClaudeAdapterV2.ts (10,417), ChatView.tsx (8,994), provider-acp adapter.ts (8,514), CodexAdapterV2.ts (7,528)
reengineering.gain: Smaller units for review and for agent context, and fewer merge conflicts in a very high-PR-volume repo.
reengineering.measure: Non-test source files over 3,000 lines drop from 26 to 10 or fewer, with maximum file size tracked per release by a CI size budget.

reengineering.gain: Lower per-turn context cost and better tool selection for every provider session.
reengineering.measure: tools/list bytes per session type are measured in CI. Baseline: at least 38,362 description characters across 83 tools. Target: 50% or less for sessions with no preview or device attached.

questions: Does the durable orchestration kernel avoid repeating side effects after a crash? Mostly yes. Commits happen in one transaction, receipts deduplicate commands, replay-safe effects are requeued and process-bound ones cancelled, and auto-resume is capped at 3 (EffectOutbox.ts:123-142,496-530; RestartContinuation.ts:33). Remaining risks: a documented power-loss window (synchronous=NORMAL) and no abrupt-kill fault injection.

Is telemetry consent a red line (PRV-1 at 1 or below)? No. Use is disclosed in a docs page, a first-run notice and the privacy policy, and no prompts or content are sent. It scores 2: on by default, opt-out only by environment variable, no DO_NOT_TRACK, and an 'anonymous' label despite linkable hashed provider-account ids.

Are agents run with least agency by default? No for threads: the default is Full access, which maps to Codex dangerFullAccess with approvals off and to Claude bypassPermissions, with no T3 sandbox. Yes for outside MCP agents, which default to read-only with mode ceilings and per-tool access classes.
not_examined: Runtime behaviour: nothing was built or run (static review), so there was no oracle run, quickstart run or latency measurement.
Git history: the shallow clone has 1 commit, so contributor concentration, release cadence and breaking-change rate were not measured.
Branch-protection and required-review settings, GitHub secret scanning and published advisories, all configured outside the repo.
infra/relay (Cloudflare Worker, Postgres, Clerk) beyond notification payloads and monitoring queries.
apps/mobile native modules (Swift/Kotlin), native/* Rust and C helpers, and the vendored libghostty binaries.
Whether tsc-rs enforces the Effect language-service diagnostics during CI typecheck.
Whether the background-service log file captures the one-time startup pairing URL printed to stdout.
CSRF and WebSocket-origin posture of cookie-authenticated endpoints under the production wildcard CORS policy (apps/server/src/http.ts:258-275).
Main-process validation of IPC messages from preview webview guests that run without context isolation (apps/desktop/src/preview/PickPreload.ts).
.repos/ vendored reference subtrees (skipped by the probes and by this review).
scope_notes: agent-harness: T3 Code runs provider coding agents (Codex, Claude, Cursor, Grok, OpenCode, Pi, ACP) that execute commands on the user's machine and serves them to web, desktop and mobile clients over a local server (127.0.0.1:3773), MCP and a cloud relay. All flags are set except heavy_compute, because model inference happens at the providers. This is a static review of commit 7e289ae1 (shallow clone), excluding the vendored .repos/ trees.
